extracted.intended_audience: prospective ARPA-H applicants / research teams preparing proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how ARPA‑H evaluates funding proposals, including the agency's core merit criteria (technical, health impact, cost-effectiveness), solicitation‑specific criteria, and the Heilmeier Catechism questions applicants should address.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Review Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: ARPA-H conducts impartial, equitable, comprehensive proposal reviews based on the evaluation criteria listed in each solicitation, then selects the performers whose proposed solution meets ARPA-H's technical, policy, and programmatic goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are merit-based and consider fit to ARPA‑H technical, policy, and programmatic objectives; read solicitation criteria carefully because they drive the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the proposal's scientific and technical quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: Innovation and scientific soundness; Likelihood of achieving stated technical goals; Quality of methodology. Reviewers evaluate whether the approach is technically credible and likely to achieve the claimed outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Health Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the magnitude and practical significance of the proposed work for public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: Magnitude of potential public health benefit; Path to deployment and adoption; Equitable distribution of benefits. Emphasis on real-world health outcomes, scalability, and fairness of benefit distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the budget and resource use relative to expected benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: Realism of proposed budget; Cost-benefit analysis; Efficient use of resources. Reviewers judge whether costs are justified by projected impact and whether funds are used efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation-Specific Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submission is evaluated against the criteria outlined in the specific solicitation to which it responds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations may define additional or different evaluation criteria; applicants must read the solicitation carefully as criteria vary and can override/augment general criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Question 1 — What are you trying to do?
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate your objectives using absolutely no jargon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central to ARPA‑H's approach; clarity and non‑jargon explanation of objectives are expected when engaging with Program Managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Question 2 — How is it done today, and what are the limits of current practice?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain current state-of-the-art practices and their limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect a clear characterization of existing approaches and why they are insufficient for the proposed goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Question 3 — What is new in your approach and why do you think it will be successful?
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe novelty in approach and rationale for expected success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must justify innovation and provide credible arguments/evidence for why the proposed approach can overcome current limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Question 4 — Who cares? If you are successful, what difference will it make?
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify stakeholders and describe the expected difference/impact of success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie technical outcomes to meaningful stakeholders and measurable benefits; link to public health impact and deployment/adoption pathways where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Question 5 — What are the risks?
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify technical, programmatic, and other risks to success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide honest risk assessment and, where possible, mitigation strategies or contingency plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Question 6 — How much will it cost?
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide realistic cost estimates for carrying out the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budgets should be realistic and supportable; cost details feed into the Cost‑Effectiveness evaluation criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Question 7 — How long will it take?
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify the timeline and schedule for accomplishing objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include milestones and timing; reviewers use timeline information to judge feasibility and to define mid‑term/final assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heilmeier Question 8 — What are the mid-term and final 'exams' to check for success?
rubrics_metrics.description: Define measurable milestones or tests to determine progress and success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, assessable milestones (mid‑term and final) that reviewers can use to evaluate progress and make go/no‑go decisions.
